title: Publication bias
text:
We evaluate small-study effects and time-lag patterns for lnRR. We use the same sampling variance-covariance matrix and random-effects structure as the overall-effect model.






NoteVariable definitions










Variable
Definition




sqrt_inv_e_n
Square root of the inverse effective sample size, calculated as \(\sqrt{1/n_{ex} + 1/n_c}\).


publication_year
Publication year extracted from study_id.


year_c
Publication year centred on the mean publication year.






Analysis data and overall model
We load the effect-size database and reconstruct the complete VCV matrix with the same metafor::vcalc() specification used in Chapter 3. We then fit the intercept-only model that provides the centre line for the funnel plot.

# Load the lnRR effect sizes and sampling variances.
db <- readr::read_csv(
  file.path(derived_dir, "db_effect_sizes.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Extract the four-digit publication year from study_id.
db <- db |>
  mutate(
    publication_year = as.integer(
      stringr::str_extract(study_id, "(19|20)[0-9]{2}")
    )
  )

if (anyNA(db$publication_year)) {
  stop("A publication year could not be extracted from study_id.")
}

# Construct the complete sampling VCV matrix.
VCV_lnRR <- metafor::vcalc(
  vi = lnRR_var,
  cluster = study_id,
  grp1 = ex_id,
  grp2 = con_id,
  w1 = ex_n,
  w2 = c_n,
  obs = es_id,
  rho = 0.5,
  data = db
)

# Fit the intercept-only multilevel model.
ma_all <- metafor::rma.mv(
  yi = lnRR,
  V = VCV_lnRR,
  random = list(
    ~ 1 | study_id,
    ~ 1 | es_id,
    ~ 1 | strain
  ),
  test = "t",
  method = "REML",
  sparse = TRUE,
  data = db
)

summary(ma_all)

#> 
#> Multivariate Meta-Analysis Model (k = 207; method: REML)
#> 
#>    logLik   Deviance        AIC        BIC       AICc

Visual inspection: funnel plot
We plot lnRR against inverse standard error. Greater values on the vertical axis represent greater precision.

# Draw the inverse-SE funnel plot.
metafor::funnel(
  ma_all,
  yaxis = "seinv",
  las = 1,
  digits = c(2, 1),
  xlab = "Standardised residuals (lnRR)",
  ylab = "Precision (inverse of SE)",
  pch = 21,
  bg = scales::alpha("black", 0.2),
  col = "black",
  cex = 1.2
)










Egger-type regression
We test small-study effects with an N-based precision term. This avoids using the sampling standard error as the predictor because lnRR and its sampling variance are mathematically related (Nakagawa et al. 2022).

# Calculate the N-based precision term for every effect size.
dt_egger_full <- db |>
  mutate(
    sqrt_inv_e_n = sqrt((1 / ex_n) + (1 / c_n))
  )

# Fit the Egger-type multilevel meta-regression.
egger_model_full <- metafor::rma.mv(
  yi = lnRR,
  V = VCV_lnRR,
  mods = ~ 1 + sqrt_inv_e_n,
  random = list(
    ~ 1 | study_id,
    ~ 1 | es_id,
    ~ 1 | strain
  ),
  test = "t",
  method = "REML",
  sparse = TRUE,
  data = dt_egger_full
)

summary(egger_model_full)

We display the fitted relationship between lnRR and the N-based precision term.

egger_plot <- orchaRd::bubble_plot(
  egger_model_full,
  mod = "sqrt_inv_e_n",
  group = "study_id",
  xlab = "Square root of inverse effective sample size",
  ylab = "Effect size (lnRR)"
)

egger_plot










Time-lag pattern
We use publication year to test whether lnRR estimates change systematically over time. This analysis evaluates a time-lag or decline pattern, in which effect-size estimates differ between earlier and later publications. We include the N-based precision term in the same model so we can estimate the publication-year coefficient while accounting for differences in effective sample size. We centre publication year on its mean so the model intercept represents the expected lnRR at the average publication year. The model retains the same VCV matrix and random-effects structure.

# Centre publication year on its mean.
db_decline <- dt_egger_full |>
  mutate(
    year_c = publication_year - mean(publication_year)
  )

# Fit publication year and the precision term in the same model.
year_lag_model <- metafor::rma.mv(
  yi = lnRR,
  V = VCV_lnRR,
  mods = ~ 1 + year_c + sqrt_inv_e_n,
  random = list(
    ~ 1 | study_id,
    ~ 1 | es_id,
    ~ 1 | strain
  ),
  test = "t",
  method = "REML",
  sparse = TRUE,
  data = db_decline
)

summary(year_lag_model)

#> Multivariate Meta-Analysis Model (k = 207; method: REML)

We display the fitted relationship between lnRR and publication year while retaining the precision term in the model.

# Draw the bubble plot on the centred-year scale.
time_lag_plot <- orchaRd::bubble_plot(
  year_lag_model,
  mod = "year_c",
  group = "study_id",
  xlab = "Year of publication",
  ylab = "Effect size (lnRR)"
)

# Replace centred values with publication years on the horizontal axis.
mean_year <- mean(db_decline$publication_year)
target_years <- pretty(range(db_decline$publication_year), n = 6)
target_years <- target_years[
  target_years >= min(db_decline$publication_year) &
    target_years <= max(db_decline$publication_year)
]

time_lag_plot <- time_lag_plot +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = target_years - mean_year,
    labels = target_years,
    name = "Year of publication"
  )

time_lag_plot










Small-study and time-lag plots
We combine the two regression plots in one figure.

publication_bias_dashboard <- egger_plot / time_lag_plot +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.tag = ggplot2::element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
  )

publication_bias_dashboard








We treat these diagnostics as exploratory because the effect sizes are heterogeneous and statistically dependent. We consider them together because each examines a different pattern, and we do not treat any single diagnostic as conclusive evidence of publication bias.

title: Effect size calculation
text:
Data types

We calculate non-percentage outcomes on their extracted scale.
We apply an arcsine-square-root transformation before calculating percentage outcomes.

title: Effect size calculation
text:
Boundary corrections

For non-percentage outcomes, we replace a zero mean with 0.9 times the smallest positive mean in the same outcome stratum.
For all outcomes, we replace a zero SD with the smallest positive SD for the same treatment arm and outcome stratum.
For percentage outcomes, we replace means of 0 and 100 with 0.5 and 99.5, respectively.

We define an outcome stratum with assay_type, measurement_variable, data_type, and data_units.

title: Effect size calculation
text:
Comparison structure

For comparison_structure == "independent", we use metafor::escalc(measure = "ROM").
For comparison_structure == "dependent", we use metafor::escalc(measure = "ROMC", ri = 0.5).

title: Effect size calculation
Prenatal chronic noise exposure meta-analysis
text:
What this site contains
This online supplement provides the computational workflow for the systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis of prenatal chronic noise exposure and offspring behavioural outcomes in laboratory rodents.
It includes:

preparation of the analysis database from the original extraction file;
calculation of the log response ratio (lnRR) and its sampling variance;
construction of the sampling variance-covariance matrix;
estimation of the overall lnRR with a multilevel intercept-only model;
separate multilevel meta-regressions for the planned moderators;
publication-bias diagnostics for small-study effects and time-lag patterns.



How to navigate

Data preparation calculates missing statistics and creates the two derived databases.
Effect size calculation calculates lnRR and lnRR_var and reports their distributions.
Sampling variance-covariance matrix constructs and checks V with metafor.
Overall effect fits the intercept-only multilevel meta-analytic model.
Uni-moderators subsets V and fits one multilevel meta-regression for each moderator.
Publication bias displays the funnel plot and fits the small-study and publication-year models.



Reproducibility
We run all data preparation and analyses in R through Quarto. We read the original extraction file without overwriting it. Each chapter creates the data or model object required by the following chapter.

title: Data preparation
text:
Calculation methods

We estimate a missing mean from Q1, the median, Q3, and sample size with the Luo et al. method (Luo et al. 2018).
We estimate a missing SD from Q1, Q3, and sample size with the Wan et al. method (Wan et al. 2014).
When the source reports an SE but not an SD, we calculate SD = SE × sqrt(n).
When the source does not report an SE, we calculate SE = SD / sqrt(n).
We retain existing extracted values unchanged.

\[
\widehat{M} =
\left(0.7 + \frac{0.39}{n}\right)\frac{Q_1 + Q_3}{2}
+ \left(0.3 - \frac{0.39}{n}\right)M_d
\]
\[
\widehat{SD} =
\frac{Q_3-Q_1}
{2\Phi^{-1}\left(\frac{0.75n-0.125}{n+0.25}\right)}
\]
We define one function for each published estimator and one function that completes the mean, SD, and SE for either treatment arm. The function also records the source of every analysis value.

estimate_mean_luo <- function(q1, median, q3, n) {
  weight <- 0.7 + 0.39 / n
  weight * ((q1 + q3) / 2) + (1 - weight) * median
}

estimate_sd_wan <- function(q1, q3, n) {
  denominator <- 2 * stats::qnorm((0.75 * n - 0.125) / (n + 0.25))
  (q3 - q1) / denominator
}

complete_arm_statistics <- function(data, arm) {
  n <- data[[paste0(arm, "_n")]]
  mean_source <- data[[paste0(arm, "_mean")]]
  sd_source <- data[[paste0(arm, "_sd")]]
  se_source <- data[[paste0(arm, "_se")]]
  median <- data[[paste0(arm, "_median")]]
  q1 <- data[[paste0(arm, "_q1")]]
  q3 <- data[[paste0(arm, "_q3")]]

  mean_from_iqr <- is.na(mean_source) & complete.cases(q1, median, q3, n)
  sd_from_iqr <- is.na(sd_source) & complete.cases(q1, q3, n)
  sd_from_se <- is.na(sd_source) & !sd_from_iqr & !is.na(se_source) & !is.na(n)

  if (any(mean_from_iqr & !(q1 <= median & median <= q3))) {
    stop("Invalid Q1 <= median <= Q3 ordering in the ", arm, " arm.")
  }

  mean_analysis <- mean_source
  mean_analysis[mean_from_iqr] <- estimate_mean_luo(
    q1[mean_from_iqr], median[mean_from_iqr], q3[mean_from_iqr], n[mean_from_iqr]
  )

  sd_analysis <- sd_source
  sd_analysis[sd_from_iqr] <- estimate_sd_wan(
    q1[sd_from_iqr], q3[sd_from_iqr], n[sd_from_iqr]
  )
  sd_analysis[sd_from_se] <- se_source[sd_from_se] * sqrt(n[sd_from_se])

  se_analysis <- se_source
  se_from_sd <- is.na(se_analysis) & !is.na(sd_analysis) & !is.na(n)
  se_analysis[se_from_sd] <- sd_analysis[se_from_sd] / sqrt(n[se_from_sd])

  data[[paste0(arm, "_mean_analysis")]] <- mean_analysis
  data[[paste0(arm, "_mean_method")]] <- if_else(
    mean_from_iqr,
    "Luo et al. (2018): Q1, median, Q3, and n",
    "Extracted mean used unchanged"
  )
  data[[paste0(arm, "_sd_analysis")]] <- sd_analysis
  data[[paste0(arm, "_sd_method")]] <- case_when(
    sd_from_iqr ~ "Wan et al. (2014): Q1, Q3, and n",
    sd_from_se ~ "SD = SE * sqrt(n)",
    TRUE ~ "Extracted SD used unchanged"
  )
  data[[paste0(arm, "_se_analysis")]] <- se_analysis
  data[[paste0(arm, "_se_method")]] <- if_else(
    se_from_sd,
    "SE = SD / sqrt(n)",
    "Extracted SE used unchanged"
  )

  if (anyNA(mean_analysis) || anyNA(sd_analysis) || anyNA(se_analysis)) {
    stop("Unresolved summary statistic in the ", arm, " arm.")
  }

  data
}

We apply the functions to the control arm (c) and then to the exposed arm (ex). We summarise the calculation methods by arm and statistic.

with_statistics <- source_for_derivation |>
  complete_arm_statistics("c") |>
  complete_arm_statistics("ex")

method_counts <- bind_rows(
  with_statistics |> count(arm = "Control", statistic = "Mean", method = c_mean_method, name = "rows"),

Data checks
We check the identifiers, summary statistics, sample sizes, and coded variables before exporting the analysis-ready database. The chapter stops if any check fails.

  ),
  failures = c(
    sum(is.na(analysis_ready$es_id)) + sum(duplicated(analysis_ready$es_id)),

title: Sampling variance-covariance matrix
text:
We construct the sampling variance-covariance matrix from the lnRR sampling variances and the exposed- and control-group identifiers in the extraction database.
We first load the effect-size database and check the columns required to construct V.






NoteVariable definitions










Variable
Definition




study_id
Identifier for the primary research paper and the cluster argument in vcalc().


es_id
Unique identifier for each effect size.


ex_id
Identifier for an exposed group within an experiment and study.


con_id
Identifier for a control group within an experiment and study.


out_id
Identifier for a behavioural outcome.


ex_n, c_n
Exposed- and control-group sample sizes.


lnRR_var
Sampling variance of lnRR and the diagonal value of V.


V
Sampling variance-covariance matrix for the lnRR estimates.


\(\rho\)
Working correlation for multiple or repeated outcomes that share a group.






pacman::p_load(
  dplyr,
  knitr,
  metafor,
  readr,
  tibble
)

project_root <- normalizePath("..", mustWork = TRUE)
derived_dir <- file.path(project_root, "Data", "derived")

# Load the effect-size database from Chapter 2.
vcv_data <- readr::read_csv(
  file.path(derived_dir, "db_effect_sizes.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# List the variables required to construct V and its index.
required_columns <- c(
  "study_id", "es_id", "ex_id", "con_id", "out_id",
  "ex_n", "c_n", "lnRR", "lnRR_var"
)

if (length(setdiff(required_columns, names(vcv_data))) > 0) {
  stop("Required columns are missing from the effect-size database.")
}
if (anyDuplicated(vcv_data$es_id)) {
  stop("es_id must be unique before constructing V.")
}
if (anyNA(vcv_data[c("study_id", "es_id", "ex_id", "con_id")])) {
  stop("Study and group identifiers must be complete before constructing V.")
}
if (any(!is.finite(vcv_data$lnRR_var)) || any(vcv_data$lnRR_var <= 0)) {
  stop("lnRR_var must contain positive finite sampling variances.")
}
if (any(vcv_data$ex_n <= 0) || any(vcv_data$c_n <= 0)) {
  stop("Group sample sizes must be positive before constructing V.")
}


Matrix construction
We use metafor::vcalc() to construct V (Viechtbauer 2010). We use study_id as the study cluster, ex_id and con_id as the contrasted-group identifiers, and ex_n and c_n as the group weights. We supply each es_id as a distinct observation. For multiple or repeated outcomes that share an exposed or control group, we use a working correlation of \(\rho = 0.5\). We assign zero sampling covariance to effect sizes that share neither group.

# Set the fixed working correlation.
working_rho <- 0.5

# Construct the sampling variance-covariance matrix.
V <- metafor::vcalc(
  vi = lnRR_var,
  cluster = study_id,
  grp1 = ex_id,
  grp2 = con_id,
  w1 = ex_n,
  w2 = c_n,
  obs = es_id,
  rho = working_rho,
  checkpd = TRUE,
  data = vcv_data
)

# Label the matrix rows and columns with es_id.
dimnames(V) <- list(vcv_data$es_id, vcv_data$es_id)



Matrix checks
We check the diagonal, finite values, symmetry, dependency pattern, and positive definiteness of V before exporting it.

# Identify effect-size pairs from the same study that share either group.
same_study <- outer(vcv_data$study_id, vcv_data$study_id, `==`)
shared_exposed_group <- same_study &
  outer(vcv_data$ex_id, vcv_data$ex_id, `==`)
shared_control_group <- same_study &
  outer(vcv_data$con_id, vcv_data$con_id, `==`)
shared_group <- shared_exposed_group | shared_control_group
diag(shared_group) <- FALSE

# Identify effect-size pairs with non-zero covariance.
nonzero_covariance <- abs(V) > sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)
diag(nonzero_covariance) <- FALSE

# Use the smallest eigenvalue to check positive definiteness.
minimum_eigenvalue <- min(eigen(V, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values)

vcv_checks <- tibble(
  check = c(
    "Matrix rows",
    "Matrix columns",
    "Diagonal equals lnRR_var",
    "Finite matrix entries",
    "Symmetric matrix",
    "Positive-definite matrix",
    "Effect-size pairs with non-zero covariance",
    "Non-zero covariance pairs without a shared group"
  ),
  value = c(
    as.character(nrow(V)),
    as.character(ncol(V)),
    as.character(max(abs(diag(V) - vcv_data$lnRR_var)) < sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)),
    as.character(all(is.finite(V))),
    as.character(isSymmetric(V)),
    as.character(minimum_eigenvalue > 0),
    as.character(sum(upper.tri(V) & nonzero_covariance)),
    as.character(sum(upper.tri(V) & nonzero_covariance & !shared_group))
  )
)

title: Uni-moderators
text: We fit one uni-moderator multilevel meta-regression for each study characteristic. Every model uses lnRR as the response and the same random-effects structure as the overall-effect model: study (study_id), effect size (es_id), and strain (strain). We construct the complete VCV matrix with rho = 0.5. For categorical moderators, we remove levels with fewer than five effect sizes (\(k < 5\)) and subset the corresponding rows and columns of the VCV matrix.

title: Uni-moderators
Uni-moderators
text:
Fit one uni-moderator model
The function below prepares one moderator, subsets the complete VCV matrix, and fits its model. For categorical moderators with at least three retained levels, it also calculates unadjusted Tukey contrasts with a separate no-intercept model.

fit_unimoderator <- function(
  data,
  V,
  moderator,
  label,
  kind,
  missing_label = NA_character_,
  min_k = 5
) {
  # Apply the appropriate preparation rule for the moderator type.
  prepared <- if (kind == "categorical") {
    prepare_categorical(data, V, moderator, missing_label, min_k)
  } else {
    prepare_continuous(data, V, moderator)
  }

  model_data <- prepared$data
  V_subset <- prepared$V

  # Fit one multilevel meta-regression with the subsetted VCV matrix.
  model <- metafor::rma.mv(
    yi = lnRR,
    V = V_subset,
    mods = reformulate(moderator),
    random = list(
      ~ 1 | study_id,
      ~ 1 | es_id,
      ~ 1 | strain
    ),
    test = "t",
    method = "REML",
    sparse = TRUE,
    data = model_data
  )

  # Draw an orchard plot for a categorical moderator. We draw continuous
  # moderators with metafor::regplot() when we display the model results.
  model_plot <- if (kind == "categorical") {
    orchaRd::orchard_plot(
      model,
      mod = moderator,
      group = "study_id",
      xlab = "lnRR",
      flip = TRUE,
      angle = 0,
      legend.pos = "top.left"
    )
  } else {
    NULL
  }

  contrasts <- NULL

  # Calculate unadjusted Tukey contrasts when at least three levels remain.
  if (kind == "categorical" && nlevels(model_data[[moderator]]) >= 3) {
    # Fit a no-intercept model so that each coefficient represents one level.
    no_intercept_model <- metafor::rma.mv(
      yi = lnRR,
      V = V_subset,
      mods = reformulate(moderator, intercept = FALSE),
      random = list(
        ~ 1 | study_id,
        ~ 1 | es_id,
        ~ 1 | strain
      ),
      test = "t",
      method = "REML",
      sparse = TRUE,
      data = model_data
    )

    # Create all pairwise Tukey contrasts among the retained levels.
    contrast_matrix <- multcomp::contrMat(
      table(model_data[[moderator]]),
      type = "Tukey"
    )
    colnames(contrast_matrix) <- names(coef(no_intercept_model))

    # Report the unadjusted p-value for each contrast.
    contrasts <- summary(
      multcomp::glht(no_intercept_model, linfct = contrast_matrix),
      test = multcomp::adjusted("none")
    )
  }

  list(
    variable = moderator,
    label = label,
    kind = kind,
    data = model_data,
    V = V_subset,
    level_counts = prepared$level_counts,
    model = model,
    r2 = orchaRd::r2_ml(model),
    plot = model_plot,
    contrasts = contrasts
  )
}
